sample_size.notes: Small sample — this is a RARE pattern, but the most powerful continuation signal in Bulkowski's catalog.

target_calculation.description: Target = breakout + flagpole height. The flagpole is the near-vertical 100%+ rise preceding the tight consolidation.

ultimate_high_method.definition: Highest price after upward breakout before 20% reversal

failure_definition.description: Break-even failure: price fails to rise 5% above the flag consolidation high after breakout.

failure_rate.notes: ZERO percent break-even failure in BOTH markets — this is UNPRECEDENTED in Bulkowski's statistics. HTF is the most reliable bullish continuation pattern.

post_breakout_measurement.lookahead_note: Median ~32 days. HTF resolves FAST (within 1-2 months).

performance_statistics.busted_pattern_performance: N/A — Bulkowski could not find busted HTF examples in the dataset.
performance_statistics.rank_in_bulkowski_catalog: STRONGEST performer by failure rate (0%); top 3 by average rise.

detection_signature_hint.flagpole: Near-vertical rise of 100%+ over 1-2 months (often 90-200% in 8 weeks).
detection_signature_hint.consolidation: Tight sideways consolidation for 4-5 weeks, max 20-25% retracement of flagpole.
detection_signature_hint.volume: Volume DRIES UP during consolidation, then spikes on breakout.

notes: PDF source: Encyclopedia of Chart Patterns (2nd ed.), chapter 22, p373-397, Table 22.2.
CRITICAL: HTF has 0% break-even failure in BOTH markets — UNPRECEDENTED. This is the MOST RELIABLE bullish continuation pattern in Bulkowski's catalog.
Legacy digitized folder only has flags_digitized.json (general bull/bear flags) — NO specific high_tight_flags spec. This file is the FIRST spec for HTF.
Sample size is small (307) because HTF is RARE — only forms after explosive 100%+ runs (e.g., biotech breakouts, meme stocks).
Detection requires explicit flagpole detection — must NOT trigger on regular flags. Use flagpole_height_pct >= 100 as primary filter.
Detector in legacy folder uses temporal lookahead=120 as placeholder — PDF says 32 days actual. Replace with this spec's value.
